To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a new type of optical resonator with an ultralow modal volume, and that we experimentally demonstrated this new resonator and showed that it has a very large quality factor.
we experimentally demonstrated an ultralow loss optical resonator with an ultralow volume mode.
we experimentally demonstrated deep-subwavelength localization of light with record low losses in dielectric optical cavities by incorporating subwahellength features in photonic crystal unit cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental understanding and development of novel photonic crystal structures for applications in nanophotonics.
the design and experimental realization of photonic crystals that support subwavelength optical modes with ultrahigh quality factors and ultralow losses in the near- and mid-infrared.
the development of novel optical devices based on photonic crystal cavities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work demonstrates the experimental realization of a deep-subwavelength dielectric optical resonator with a quality factor of 2.5 x 10^4, which is 2 orders of magnitude greater than the quality factor demonstrated in plasmonic bowtie resonators.
the work is a very nice demonstration of a deep subwavelength dielectric cavity.
we have demonstrated a dielectric optical cavity that supports record low mode volumes and high quality factors, which is an important step towards the strong light-matter coupling regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed and demonstrated a new approach to achieving deep-subwavelength localization of light with ultralow losses, that has the potential to enable higher-efficiency solar cell and light source technologies.
we have demonstrated that the dielectric bowtie structure can support deep-subwavelength mode volumes, with a quality factor of over 10,000, and a mode volume of only 0.03(λ/n)3.
the combination of a subwavelength cavity size and a high Q factor is a very promising route for achieving high-efficiency light sources, modulators, solar cells, and other optoelectronic devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of subwavelength mode volumes and high-quality factors is not limited to plasmonic resonances and can be achieved in dielectric structures.
dielectrics can be used for strong confinement, which is not possible with metals.
it is possible to achieve deep-subwavelength mode volumes in dielectric resonators with ultralow losses, and that these structures can be fabricated in a scalable way.
